transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (LumenHead), Tom Reed (Lumen SRE), Maya Lopez (Lumen ML)

Auto-summary (auto):
- Discovery to scope a short pilot: smoke test of embed fanout + rerank with VPC/private control plane.
- Key constraints: 2-3k QPS spikes, P95 latency target 300ms for first-pass embed fanout, rerank budget per request ~60ms, data residency and KMS required.
- Next: Redwood to send cost scenarios and benchmark harness; customer to provide sample docs and confirm timeline.

Topics:
- Current stack & pain (vector DB + elastic fallback)
- Fanout vs single-pass rerank tradeoffs
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) ops + security
- Throughput, embedding dims, quantization, caching
- Pilot success criteria and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00:03] Jordan Lee: All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, I'll be the AE on this. Marco from SE will cover the nitty gritty. Aisha, thanks for setting this up.
[00:00:12] Aisha Khan: Yeah thanks, we appreciate it. We're trying to scope a quick smoke test to validate throughput for our search reranker pipeline.
[00:00:18] Marco Alvarez: Awesome. Quick ground rules — we'll ask about your current infra, qps patterns, tail latency, what success looks like. Then we'll walk options: hosted, dedicated, private VPC.
[00:00:28] Tom Reed: Quick note, I'm here to make sure networking and SRE constraints are clear. We can't expose PII-ish logs outside of our VPC.
[00:00:35] Maya Lopez: And I'll represent the model/embedding side — dims, vector store, that sort of thing.
[00:00:40] Jordan Lee: Great. To start, can you sketch current flow? Where are embeddings computed, what vector DB, and how rerank happens?
[00:00:48] Aisha Khan: Sure. Today we compute 768-d embeddings using an internal encoder (based on open model), store in Milvus cluster. First-pass returns top-200, we do a BERT-based rerank on the application side. We're seeing some tail latency spikes during end-of-day indexing and user peak (US morning).
[00:01:02] Tom Reed: Peak we see around 2.5k QPS sustained for 10-15 minutes, 5k spikes in sudden promos.
[00:01:08] Marco Alvarez: Ok that helps. Two broad approaches for Redwood: fanout-first (embed fanout across vector db + rerank on our runtime) vs hybrid (topk from vector DB then rerank on smaller batch). Which are you leaning toward?
[00:01:20] Maya Lopez: We were excited by fanout because it reduces complexity, but worried about cost and tail latency. Our reranker is expensive.
[00:01:28] Jordan Lee: Right — fanout gives you high recall but increases per-request token work. Hybrid/topk minimizes rerank cost but can miss recall. We usually recommend a two-stage: cheap embed-first topk (e.g., 200) then a lightweight reranker on Redwood's runtime or dedicated hosts.
[00:01:40] Aisha Khan: Does Redwood support running the reranker in our VPC? We need to ensure no data leaves our network.
[00:01:45] Marco Alvarez: Yes — we have Private deployments: control plane is customer-managed and inference hosts run in your VPC or on-prem. You can bring your own KMS/HSM. We also offer Dedicated pools if you want predictable throughput but still hosted by Redwood in your account.
[00:01:58] Tom Reed: What's the difference between Dedicated and Private for network egress?
[00:02:03] Jordan Lee: Dedicated is Redwood-managed infra but isolated tenancy (reserved GPUs). With Dedicated we can enable VPC peering and strict egress rules, but secrets live in Redwood. Private is the full customer-managed deployment where the control plane is in your network and we ship an appliance/helm chart — keys and logs stay with you.
[00:02:18] Tom Reed: Got it. That matters for compliance. We need KMS integration and log audit retention in-house for the pilot.
[00:02:24] Marco Alvarez: Totally. For the smoke test we often do a Private trial or a Dedicated with strict network controls depending on timeline. Private takes a bit longer to stand up but gives you full isolation.
[00:02:34] Maya Lopez: Timeline: we want results before end of month — is Private realistic?
[00:02:38] Jordan Lee: For a minimal smoke test, Dedicated with VPC peering plus bring-your-own-KMS is usually fastest (3–7 days). Private can be done in 2–3 weeks depending on procurement.
[00:02:48] Aisha Khan: Okay that's useful. Let's talk numbers: our P95 goal for first-pass is about 300ms; rerank overall p95 target 600ms.
[00:02:56] Marco Alvarez: Those are achievable but depend on embedding dims, vector DB latency, and batch sizes. For 768-d vectors, throughput is higher than 1536-d. Also quantized models can cut latency but may affect quality.
[00:03:10] Tom Reed: We currently use FP16 encoders and raw Milvus queries take ~50ms median, 180ms p95 under load.
[00:03:17] Marco Alvarez: If Milvus p95 is 180ms then your end-to-end with a 200 topk plus rerank will add rerank time; if rerank is heavy BERT it could push you over your target. One approach: use a small re-ranker model on the first pass (cheap distilled model), then full rerank offline or cached for frequent queries.
[00:03:30] Maya Lopez: How does Redwood caching work? Could we cache KV prefixes or rerank results?
[00:03:34] Jordan Lee: We do prefix/KV cache for decoding and request-level caching. For rerank, you can cache the top-k embeddings or rerank outputs for repeated queries. Redwood Optimize can surface suggestions on cache TTLs based on your traffic pattern.
[00:03:45] Aisha Khan: For the pilot we want to see: (1) ability to handle 3k sustained QPS for queries that lead to 200 topk fanout, (2) end-to-end latency numbers, (3) cost per 10k queries.
[00:03:56] Jordan Lee: Perfect — we'll map those to three benchmark scenarios: baseline (1k), typical (3k), spike (5k). We'll run them against hosted/dedicated/private cost models and send you a spreadsheet.
[00:04:08] Tom Reed: On security — can you confirm SOC2 and ISO status? Also we need network diagrams and details about audit logs retention.
[00:04:14] Marco Alvarez: Redwood is SOC2 Type II and we have ISO docs; I'll attach the compliance pack and a network diagram showing VPC peering and private deployment options. Logs can be pushed to your syslog/S3 in Private; in Dedicated we can forward audit logs to your tenant.
[00:04:28] Chris Patel: Quick interjection — what about vendor lock? If we invest in a rerank pipeline on Redwood, can we export model artifacts and metrics if we decide to move?
[00:04:35] Jordan Lee: You maintain model artifacts on your side. For outputs and metrics we can export traces, token-level cost breakdowns, and eval results. No lock-in for data — we provide exports.
[00:04:45] Aisha Khan: Good. Back to the technical: Marco, can you walk through how you would architect a fanout + rerank on Dedicated with Milvus?
[00:04:53] Marco Alvarez: Sure. High level: client query hits your service -> compute embedding (you can compute on-prem or call Redwood hosted encoder) -> call vector DB topk (Milvus) -> pass topk IDs to Redwood rerank endpoint which loads KV cache (if available) and runs reranker on dedicated GPUs -> Redwood returns ranked results. For private deployment, the whole flow stays inside your VPC. You can also colocate vector DB and Redwood hosts for low latency.
[00:05:12] Maya Lopez: When you say rerank endpoint loads KV cache, what are sizes typical? We have long docs with long contexts.
[00:05:18] Marco Alvarez: KV cache refers to model key-value attention cache for autoregressive decoding; for rerank models it's more about model weights and memory. For long doc contexts we chunk or use hierarchical embeddings. For rerank, memory is mostly model footprint; we can use sharding across GPUs for very large models.
[00:05:33] Tom Reed: What about GPU types? We currently have A100s in our infra. Redwood offers multiple GPU types?
[00:05:38] Jordan Lee: Yes — depending on Dedicated pool you can pick A100 or H100 variants. Private supports whatever you provision. For cost-sensitive running, we can run quantized FP16/INT8 variants on lower-end GPUs.
[00:05:49] Aisha Khan: If we do quantization, will it materially drop ranking relevance?
[00:05:54] Marco Alvarez: Usually small impact for many ranking tasks, but it depends. We'll include an evaluation metric in the pilot: nDCG@10 and pairwise accuracy across sample queries. If quality regressions are observed we can recommend hybrid: embed topk with small dims + higher-precision rerank on fewer items.
[00:06:10] Jordan Lee: One operational note — continuous batching helps throughput but can harm tail latency. Redwood allows you to set latency SLO and batching parameters so we respect p95 targets while maximizing throughput.
[00:06:21] Maya Lopez: That sounds useful. Can we see per-route dashboards?
[00:06:24] Marco Alvarez: Yes, Redwood Console has per-route metrics: tokens, latency, cost, traces. We can create dashboards for your rerank route and topk lookup route.
[00:06:33] Aisha Khan: For data residency, in Private we get everything on-prem. In Dedicated we need guarantees that PII doesn't leave region.
[00:06:40] Jordan Lee: We support region pinning, and with VPC peering we can control egress. I'll send the regional compliance notes.
[00:06:47] Tom Reed: On the smoke test harness — what does it look like? Can you simulate 5k spikes?
[00:06:52] Marco Alvarez: We will provide a benchmark harness (JMeter-style harness or k6) that can replay your queries at scale. For accurate fanout results, we ask you to provide a representative query set and the vector DB state snapshot (or a sample). We'll run multiple iterations and capture p50/p95/p99 and tail behavior.
[00:07:07] Jordan Lee: Also we'll instrument token-level billing estimates so you can understand cost per request under different topk and rerank configs.
[00:07:14] Aisha Khan: Good. Can we also test cold cache situations, like after an index rebuild?
[00:07:18] Marco Alvarez: Yes we typically run warm and cold cache runs to understand worst-case tail latency.
[00:07:22] Maya Lopez: A question about hybrid search — do you support reranking with semantic-plus-lexical features? For some queries we need BM25 style signals combined with embedding scores.
[00:07:31] Jordan Lee: Absolutely — we support hybrid scores. You can provide lexical features or we can compute them at query time and feed them into the reranker. Redwood Optimize can also recommend weighted combinations based on evals.
[00:07:41] Tom Reed: Ops question — what observability hooks do we get? Traces, logs, and SLO alerts?
[00:07:46] Marco Alvarez: You get tracing hooks (OpenTelemetry), per-request traces, error rates, and SLO alerting via the Console. For Private we can forward traces to your tracing backend.
[00:07:55] Speaker 1: (crosstalk)
[00:07:57] Aisha Khan: One more — do you support warm-starting rerank models and A/B testing? We want to run canary vs baseline model.
[00:08:03] Marco Alvarez: Yes, we support canary rollouts, traffic splits, and automatic fallback to a baseline if metrics regress. You can pin routes to model versions.
[00:08:12] Maya Lopez: Budget question — roughly what are costs for dedicated GPUs for this scale?
[00:08:17] Jordan Lee: I'll share a few scenarios in the spreadsheet. Roughly, for a Dedicated A100 pool sized to handle 3k sustained topk fanout with mid-size rerank you'd look at X per month (numbers in spreadsheet). We'll include per-10k-query cost and a Dedicated vs Private CAPEX/OPEX estimate.
[00:08:33] Aisha Khan: Sounds good. Any known limitations we should be aware of?
[00:08:36] Marco Alvarez: The main tradeoffs: recall vs cost for fanout, tail latency with aggressive batching, and initial setup time for Private. Also need to size your vector DB (shards) — for high qps we recommend co-locating some index replicas.
[00:08:48] Tom Reed: Regarding vector DB integration — you mentioned automatic fallback to a smaller model if vector DB is slow?
[00:08:54] Marco Alvarez: We have smart routing policies: if Milvus in region is lagging, traffic can be routed to a cached subset or alternative model variant in another region. That keeps apps online with degraded quality.
[00:09:05] Aisha Khan: Okay that's interesting. For the pilot success criteria, let's confirm: 1) p95 end-to-end under 600ms for our typical load, 2) <10% drop in nDCG@10 vs our current baseline, 3) cost within projected budget.
[00:09:16] Jordan Lee: We'll put that into the pilot plan and instrument evals accordingly.
[00:09:20] Maya Lopez: Logistics: who will run the benchmark — Redwood or Lumen?
[00:09:24] Marco Alvarez: We can run it in collaboration. For Dedicated we can run from our test harness into your VPC peering; for Private we'll provide the harness and run locally with your team.
[00:09:34] Aisha Khan: Great. Any other technical details we should capture?
[00:09:37] Jordan Lee: I'll note the following: need sample dataset (10k docs + 2k queries), confirmation of desired topk (200), reranker model size (BERT-large currently, consider distilled), region (us-east-1), compliance pack, and preferred pilot week.
[00:09:52] Chris Patel: Quick note on procurement — we'll need a one-month committed pilot order for Dedicated. Is that possible?
[00:09:58] Jordan Lee: Yes, we can do a short-term commit for pilot Dedicated capacity.
[00:10:02] Tom Reed: Network specifics — will you provide a CIDR range for peering and a runbook?
[00:10:06] Marco Alvarez: Yes, I'll attach the peering runbook and an example security group template.
[00:10:12] Aisha Khan: Cool. Anything else?
[00:10:15] Maya Lopez: Could you run a quick deep dive on how batching impacts our p95?
[00:10:19] Marco Alvarez: Sure — in brief: batching groups requests to amortize compute cost; it increases throughput but adds queueing latency. Redwood's scheduler uses latency SLOs to limit batch formation time; for p95 sensitive routes we lower max batch latency and increase dedicated concurrency. We can show charts in the pilot.
[00:10:36] Jordan Lee: Ok let's do a short run of friction items and then wrap up with action items.
[00:10:41] (discussion continues with clarifying questions, some crosstalk; transcript occasionally attributes Speaker 1)
[00:12:00] Aisha Khan: We're fine with providing a sample set and want the harness. We'll try to have sample payloads by Mar 19.
[00:12:07] Jordan Lee: Noted — Marco will send the harness repo link and sample runbook.
[00:12:12] Marco Alvarez: I'll also put a quick doc on expected GPU sizing based on your QPS and topk.
[00:12:18] Tom Reed: We'll prepare KMS paperwork.
[00:12:21] Chris Patel: I'll loop in procurement and legal for a short pilot contract.
[00:12:25] Jordan Lee: Great. Quick recap and we can capture as next steps.
[00:12:30] Jordan Lee: Recap: Redwood to send pricing scenarios, compliance pack (SOC2, ISO), network peering runbook, benchmark harness, and recommended Dedicated sizing. Lumen to provide 10k documents, 2k query set, and KMS/security contacts. Pilot week target: week of Mar 29 for a smoke test on Dedicated; Private if needed after procurement.
[00:12:52] Aisha Khan: That works for us.
[00:12:54] Maya Lopez: Thanks everyone.
[00:12:55] Jordan Lee: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invite and deliverables.
[00:13:00] (call ends)
